name: Clipboard access banner
plain: A banner or toast tells the person that an app read the clipboard.
meaning: Transparency tool. Not a gate, but caught many apps reading on launch.

android.note: Toast shown once per app read

ios.prompt_ui: Pasted from App banner at top
ios.note: Banner shows source app name; replaced by prompt from iOS 16

limits.headline: Can't hide a clipboard check, because you see a banner or toast when an app looks
limits.user_action: Nothing. The notice appears when an app looks at what you copied
can: Show you a small notice when an app looks at your clipboard
Show the source app name on iPhone in older versions
Let you notice an app that checks the clipboard on every launch
cannot: Look at your clipboard in secret while the app is in front on Android 12 and newer
Look at your clipboard in secret on iPhone with iOS 14 and newer; you see a banner or prompt
Block the app by itself; the notice only warns you
limits.differs: Android shows a toast when an app looks. iPhone showed a banner in iOS 14 and replaced it with a prompt in iOS 16.

story.what_it_is: Your phone shows a short message when an app has read what you copied.

marketing.name: Paste notification
marketing.pitch: iOS tells you when an app has pasted from another app, so you see who touches your clipboard.

marketing.name: Clipboard access toast
marketing.pitch: Android 12 and later show a small message when an app reads from the clipboard.

story.for_you: You see a small banner or toast that says 'App pasted from Other App' or similar. It appears right when it happens, so a quiet read is no longer secret. You decide whether to trust that app.
story.for_makers: Makers must now explain why they read your clipboard, since the banner is public. It scared away many sneaky reads. A well timed read after a button tap feels normal, one on launch looks suspicious.

use_cases.example: A chat app reads a copied link only after you press paste, so no banner scares you.
A game that reads copied text on every launch triggers a banner and loses trust.
A shopping app that peeks at copied text on launch would trigger a banner, so careful ones wait until you tap paste.
News apps were shown reading the clipboard on launch when the banner first appeared in 2020.
A security tool lists which apps read your clipboard, so you can spot odd behavior.
A developer uses the paste button instead, which needs no banner and no permission.

story.android_note: Android shows a toast on read, but it does not ask beforehand.
story.ios_note: iPhone shows a banner after the paste and also gates it with an Allow Paste prompt.
